resources.string: Swipe to browse, tap to review. The carousel only browses — nothing is answered here.
Requests arrive when the app opens, when you open a connection, or when you pull to refresh.
No connections yet. To add one, run pnpm pair on the computer that runs the sidecar, then tap Add connection.
Defaults used by connections unless their Rules screen overrides a section.
Last sync found more than %1$d pending requests.
The server\'s certificate isn\'t trusted, or it\'s for another host name.
This build allows plain HTTP only to 127.0.0.1.
The server no longer accepts this phone. Pair again to reconnect.
This phone no longer has the credential for this connection. Pair again to reconnect.
Live updates paused while the app is in the background.
Live updates are not configured. Refresh still works.
This sidecar must be upgraded for live updates. Refresh still works.
This sidecar advertised an incompatible live-update address. Check its configuration.
This phone\'s name on the server
Review this connection’s own rules and global defaults.
Rules highlight requests that need attention. You still approve every request.
The server revokes this phone\'s credential and cancels its pending requests. To connect again, pair with a new code.
%1$s The server still accepts this phone\'s credential until its operator runs pnpm pair revoke. Remove the connection from this phone anyway?
The server no longer accepts this phone, so there\'s nothing left to revoke.
On the computer that runs the sidecar, run pnpm pair. Then scan the QR code it shows, or enter the code printed under it.
Point the camera at the QR code.
Camera access is off, so the app can\'t scan. Enter the code instead, or allow camera access in the app\'s settings.
This phone has no camera the app can use. Enter the code instead.
That isn\'t a pairing code. Enter the whole line that starts with seekervault://pair.
That isn\'t a seeker-vault pairing code. Those start with seekervault://pair.
This pairing code is for another version of seeker-vault. Update the app or the sidecar.
The server URL in the code isn\'t valid.
The code\'s server URL doesn\'t use HTTPS. Only a debug build accepts plain HTTP, and only to 127.0.0.1 over adb reverse.
The server ID in the code isn\'t valid.
The pairing token in the code is incomplete or damaged. Copy the whole line again.
Pair only with a server you run. Whoever controls it can send this phone requests to review.
This is a development address. It reaches the computer through adb reverse.
You already have a connection to this server: %1$s. Pairing again makes a new connection, and the server revokes the old one.
%1$s uses the same address, but it\'s a different server. This code makes a separate connection.
The server refused the code: it was already used, it expired, or a newer code replaced it. Run pnpm pair again.
The server says this code was issued for a different address. Scan the code again, or check SIDECAR_PUBLIC_URL.
The server\'s certificate isn\'t trusted, or it\'s for another host name. Use a trusted HTTPS endpoint (docs/security.md).
This build allows plain HTTP only to 127.0.0.1. Run adb reverse for the sidecar\'s port.
Couldn\'t reach %1$s. Is the sidecar running, and can this phone reach that address?
The server\'s answer wasn\'t valid, so nothing was saved.
This phone couldn\'t store the credential securely, so nothing was saved.
